features.feature: View and search the attendee list
features.what: Lists everyone with a ticket or an app profile, with search, sort and paging.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Attendees.
Type a name, email or company in the search box.
Click Search.
Click a column header to sort.
features.statusNote: Rows now show name, company, title and ticket. Search still matches the email address only, and sorting by a column other than name does nothing.

features.what: Adds one person as a registration so they can be badged and checked in.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Attendees.
Click Add an attendee.
Enter Name and Email.
Pick the Ticket type.
Click Add attendee.
features.statusNote: The registration saves with the ticket type you pick, and the person can be checked in and badged. Nobody is emailed a claim code until the event has its own sending address.

features.what: Uploads or pastes a CSV, previews the rows and errors, then creates or updates registrations by email.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Attendees.
Click Import attendees.
Choose a CSV file or paste the rows.
Click Check the file.
Read the preview and the row errors.
Tick "Import the good rows anyway" if some rows are bad.
Click Import N attendees.
features.statusNote: Registrations save, and imported names and tickets show on the list, on Check-in and on Name Badges. Nobody is emailed a claim code until the event has its own sending address.

features.what: Changes an attendee’s name, email, company, title or ticket type, or cancels the registration and gives the seat back to stock. Every change is written to the audit log with who made it.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Attendees.
Click a name to open the panel, or use the three dots on the row.
Click Edit, change the fields and click Save.
To change what they hold, pick a different ticket type and save.
To take them off the event, click Cancel registration and confirm.
features.statusNote: Correcting an address keeps the same badge code, so a badge already printed still scans.

features.feature: Transfer a ticket to somebody else
features.what: Moves a registration to a different person. The new holder gets their own badge code and claim code, and the old one stops working.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Attendees.
Click the name to open the panel.
Click Transfer ticket.
Enter the new holder’s name and email address.
Click Transfer.
features.statusNote: The transfer and the new badge code work. The new holder is not emailed their ticket until the event has its own sending address, so give them the claim code yourself.

features.what: Downloads the attendee list or the badge and catering list as CSV.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Attendees.
Click Export attendees.
Pick Export basic attendee list or Export badge and catering list.
features.statusNote: The file carries name, title, company, ticket and category.

features.feature: Download everything held about one person
features.what: One file with everything held about a person: their registration, profile, saved sessions, messages, posts, survey answers and check-ins. Badge and claim codes are left out and the file says so.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Attendees.
Click the name to open the panel.
Click Download their data.
Send the file to the person who asked for it.
features.statusNote: Only the owner can do this. A check-in volunteer cannot download somebody’s conversations.

features.what: Removes a person from the event and shows, in plain words, what will go and what has to stay. A paid order is a financial record and stays, with their name taken off it. An unsubscribe stays as well, so they are not mailed again.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Attendees.
Click the name to open the panel.
Click Delete their data.
Read the list of what goes and what stays.
Type their email address and the dashboard passphrase.
Click Delete.
features.statusNote: It cannot be undone, which is why it asks for the passphrase again.

features.what: Shows app adoption, ticket mix, top companies, revenue and session attendance.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Analytics & Exports.

features.what: Downloads CSVs: attendees, catering, orders, speakers, sessions, sponsors, checked-in, session attendance, attendance hours.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Analytics & Exports.
Scroll to Exports.
Click Download on the row you need.
features.statusNote: All nine files download.

features.what: Shows the registration count. There is no cap and nothing to buy.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Attendee Limit Upgrade.
features.statusNote: Information page. No setting or purchase exists.

features.what: States that the event is in-person only.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Hybrid Settings.
features.statusNote: No settings. The data model has no stream or remote audience field.

features.what: Would compare attendance across events.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Cross-Event Report.
features.statusNote: Only one event exists, so the page shows an empty state.

features.feature: Invite a team member and set what they can open
features.what: Invites somebody to the dashboard by email. They set their own passphrase and see only the areas their roles cover: Finance, Agenda, Sponsors, Check-in only or Reviewer manager. Owner sees everything. A role decides which screens open, which buttons work and which exports download.
steps: Open Attendees > Admin Settings.
Enter the person’s name and email address.
Tick the roles they need.
Click Invite.
Copy the link shown and send it to them.
Use Change roles or Remove on their row later.
features.statusNote: Invitations, roles and the audit trail all work. The link is copied and sent by hand until the event has its own sending address. It works once and expires in three days.

features.feature: Attendee list and contact sharing switches
features.what: Two checkboxes for whether attendees can browse the list and share contact details.
steps: Open Attendees > Admin Settings.
Tick or untick the two boxes under Attendee-facing.
Click Save.
features.statusNote: The values save, but nothing reads them, so attendees see no change. Attendee messaging is switched off on Tools > Admin Control > Code Access Control instead.

features.what: Saves a short note that shows as a banner on the Check-in screen.
steps: Open Attendees > Admin Settings.
Type the note in the Check-in staff box.
Click Save.
Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Check-in to see the banner.

features.what: Keeps a list of volunteers with role, shift, status and notes, and warns about clashing shifts.
steps: Open Attendees > Call For Volunteers > Volunteer Manager.
Scroll to Add a volunteer.
Enter Name, Email and Role.
Set Status, Day, Starts and Ends.
Click Add to roster.
On a roster row, click Confirm, Declined, No-show or Remove.
features.statusNote: The roster saves. There is no public sign-up form, no email to volunteers and no edit for a saved row other than status. The roster is empty on the live project.

features.what: Shows which volunteers have signed each waiver.
steps: Open Attendees > Release & Consent Forms.
Click + New form.
Set the audience to Volunteers and the status to Published.
Click Create form.
Open Attendees > Call For Volunteers > Release & Consent Forms.
Click the waiver to see who signed.
features.statusNote: Signing links are not sent. Copy each link from the register and send it yourself. A missing waiver blocks nothing. No form and no volunteers exist on the live project, so signing was not seen end to end.

features.what: Up to twenty named categories with a colour. Assign one by hand to a person or to a selection, or set a rule on a ticket type. Categories show on the attendee list, on the name badge and in the exports.
steps: Open Attendees > Categories.
Click New category, enter the name, pick a colour and save.
To assign by hand, tick people on Attendees > Manage Attendees > Attendees and pick the category.
To assign by ticket, open Tickets > Attendee Customization > Attendee Categories.
Check the result on Attendees > Name Badges.

features.what: Groups attendees by ticket type, app adoption, directory presence and company size.
steps: Open Attendees > Segments.
Click View on a segment row.
features.statusNote: Segments are computed, not editable, and cannot be used as a message audience from here. Ticket and company groups now read real numbers.

features.what: Shows which ticket types include workshops and the video library.
steps: Open Attendees > Ticket Session Mapping.
features.statusNote: Read from the ticket type flags. Edit them in Tickets > Ticket Setup. Held by now reads real numbers. Who may take a seat in a session is set on Tickets > Ticket Setup > Session RSVP.

features.feature: Set a cap on a session
features.what: Caps how many people may take a seat in a session, against room seats and door counts. A full session sends the next person to a waitlist.
steps: Open Attendees > Session Cap.
Filter by day or search.
To change a cap, open Content > Agenda Center > Session Manager and edit the session capacity.
Set who may sign up on Tickets > Ticket Setup > Session RSVP.
features.statusNote: The cap is counted and held when somebody signs up in the app. Waiting on the new access settings being published to the live event.

features.what: Writes versioned consent forms for attendees, speakers or volunteers and tracks who signed.
steps: Open Attendees > Release & Consent Forms.
Click + New form.
Enter title, wording and audience.
Tick Required if an unsigned form should block check-in and app access.
Set status to Published.
Click Create form.
Click the form title to open its register.
Click Send signing links to email everybody who has not signed, or copy one link at a time.
features.statusNote: Forms, signatures and the block at the desk all work. The signing link goes out by email once the event has its own sending address, and until then each link is copied from the register. If two organizers press Send at the same moment, some people get the email twice. No form exists on the live event yet.

features.feature: Check in by badge scan or code
features.what: Checks a person in at the main door from a QR scan or a six-character code.
steps: Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Check-in.
Type a name in This station's name.
Click Start camera and hold up the badge, or type the code and click Check in.
Read the result panel.
features.statusNote: Camera scanning needs Chrome or Edge. Safari and Firefox fall back to typing the code. On a phone the code box and result panel are cut off.

features.what: Finds a person in the list and checks them in without a code. Can be undone.
steps: Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Check-in.
Scroll to Check in by name.
Search for the person.
Click Check in on their row.
Click Undo on the row to reverse it.
features.statusNote: Names and tickets show correctly here. On a phone only the name column fits, so the Check in button is off screen.

features.feature: Check in for a day or a session
features.what: Opens a separate list that counts people into one day or one session.
steps: Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Check-in.
Pick a day under Check-in for the day, or a session under Check-in for the session.
Click Start.
Scan or check in by name as usual.
Click the Main Door chip to go back to the event list.

features.what: Adds another named list, for example a VIP entrance.
steps: Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Check-in.
Scroll to Lists.
Enter a Name and pick a Kind.
Click Create list.

features.what: A door screen showing how many people are in, split by ticket type and by hour, updating as the desk scans.
steps: Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Check-in.
Read the arrivals panel above the desk table.
Leave the screen open on the desk through the day.

features.what: Shows recent check-ins and every scan, and downloads the checked-in list.
steps: Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Check-in.
Scroll to Recent check-ins and Scan log.
Click Export Check-in Lists.
Pick Export checked-in list (CSV) or Export session attendance (CSV).
features.statusNote: The checked-in, session attendance and full attendee files are all correct.

features.what: Opens a scanner that counts people into one session, and lists door counts per session.
steps: Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Session Self Check-in.
Pick the Session.
Enter a Station name.
Click Open the room door.
Scan badges on the screen that opens.
features.statusNote: Staff scanning works. Attendees cannot check themselves into a session from their phone.

features.what: A stripped-down scanner to leave on a tablet at the entrance.
steps: Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Kiosk Check-in.
Enter a station name and pick the list.
Click Apply.
Bookmark the address on the device.
Lock the device in kiosk mode.
features.statusNote: Scanning works. The tablet must stay signed in as an organizer, and badges do not print on scan.

features.what: Lets attendees check themselves in from their own phone.
steps: Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Self Check-in.
features.statusNote: Not available. The app’s access settings do not let an attendee check themselves in. The page points to Kiosk Check-in instead.

features.what: Shows arrivals at the main door.
steps: Open Attendees > Check-in & Checkout > Checkout.
features.statusNote: Nobody can be checked out. There is no exit record, so no live occupancy number.

features.what: Prints 3.5 x 2.25 inch badges with name, company, title, ticket and QR code, 25 to a sheet.
steps: Open Attendees > Name Badges.
Click a ticket chip or search to filter.
Click Print 25 badges.
Print from the browser dialog.
Go to the next page and repeat.
features.statusNote: Badges show real names, companies, tickets and categories. Printing is one sheet of 25 at a time. There is no badge designer, no custom fields and no print on check-in.

features.what: Issues a certificate with certified hours to everyone counted into at least one session, then prints them.
steps: Scan people into sessions first (Session Self Check-in).
Open Attendees > Certificates.
Edit Wording, Signed by and Their role.
Replace the Certificate mark if needed.
Click Issue N certificates.
Scroll to the certificates and print from the browser.
Click Download CSV for hours by attendee.
features.statusNote: Printed or saved as PDF from the browser only. Not emailed, and attendees cannot download their own. The Issue button is disabled until someone has been scanned into a session. Nobody has been on the live project, so issuing was not seen.

features.what: Explains how to move attendee data into these tools by hand.
steps: Open Attendees > Manage Attendees > Analytics & Exports.
Download the Attendee list CSV.
Import the file in Mailchimp, Constant Contact or your CRM.
features.statusNote: No connection exists for any of the three. The pages are instructions for a manual export.

uiIssues.issue: Two pages are still engineering notes with no controls: "What hybrid would actually require" and "A player in Expo Go" on Hybrid Settings, and the attendee limit page. The Self Check-in and Checkout essays have been cut.
uiIssues.fix: Cut each page to one sentence of status and a link to the screen that does the job, or hide these routes from the menu.

uiIssues.issue: Filter chips are about 20px tall and column sort links about 16px. Row buttons and menus are now 32px or more, but the chips and sort links were not covered. Seen on Check-in, Attendees, Categories, Segments, Session Cap and Name Badges.
uiIssues.fix: Give filter chips and sort links the same 32px minimum as the row actions.

uiIssues.issue: Narrow column headers break mid-word ("Roo m seat s", "Coun ted in", and "Direc tory" on the Attendees table). Room names are cut to "Tata Innovation Center Audi..." and the Room cell sits higher than the rest of the row.
uiIssues.fix: Widen those columns or shorten the labels ("Seats", "Counted"), let room names wrap, and align the cell to the middle.

uiIssues.issue: The Sessions table lists all 86 sessions with no paging. The page is about 6,500px tall on desktop and 15,000px on a phone.
uiIssues.fix: Use the same Pagination and day filter as Session Cap.

uiIssues.issue: The "yes", "not yet", "fits" and "opted out" tags are 10px and stat tile labels are 11px.
uiIssues.fix: Raise small tags and tile labels to 12px.

uiIssues.issue: Empty table cells still use a long dash across Attendees, Categories, Segments, Speaker Manager and Check-in, 28 on the attendee list alone. Check-in and Kiosk rewrite the list name at render time, so Checkout and Self Check-in still show the stored "KGC 2027 (long dash) Main Door".
uiIssues.fix: Leave empty cells blank and rename the stored list so no screen has to rewrite it.

uiIssues.issue: The kiosk table still has a Device id column of raw identifiers. The same wording was removed from the check-in screen.
uiIssues.fix: Name the device by its station name, or drop the column.

uiIssues.issue: The station name input is about 170px wide and clips its own value, showing "Tata Innovation Cent". On Check-in and Kiosk the Check in and Start camera buttons touch the "This station’s name" label with no gap, and on nearly every page the stat tiles butt against the page header card with no gap.
uiIssues.fix: Let the station input take the panel width and add the missing gaps.

uiIssues.issue: Every category card draws a solid red Delete at the same weight as the blue Save, so the destructive action is as prominent as the safe one. Sponsor Tiering does the same job with a lighter Remove.
uiIssues.fix: Make Delete a light secondary action, as on Sponsor Tiering.

uiIssues.issue: The consent form register still uses the sideways-scrolling table at phone width instead of stacked rows, so the row actions are only reachable after scrolling the table sideways. Same on the attendee list, where two columns show and emails break mid-word.
uiIssues.fix: Use the stacked row layout on these tables under 768px.
uiIssues.source: round one review, remaining problem 4; round two verification, 390 pass
